name: Locked-off / static (tripod)
definition: The camera does not move. In our 2D/2.5D work a 'still' camera still gets a tiny breathing drift so the frame is not dead (GUIDE.md).
how: Real: tripod. Planning: hold the frame and let the action move inside it.
purpose: observation, comedy timing, horror waiting, letting performance or product speak
emotional_effect: calm, objective, 'the viewer looks for the change' [CRAFT]
a still camera produced less sensorimotor (mu/beta) response than a Steadicam move in one EEG study (Heimann2019) [EVIDENCE, low-medium]
avoid_when: long holds with nothing changing on a scroll feed
rig_js: cam.set(t,{px,py,s}); cam.drift(t0,t1,3-5)
html_25d: clip-25d.html: keep cam uniform and zoom constant (e.g. zoom 1.08) - or a ±0.005 drift
ai_video_prompt: Locked-off tripod shot. [subject action]. The camera does not move.
wan_prompt: static camera, tripod shot, the camera stays still, only [subject] moves
kling_setting: camera control off / all axes 0 (if the UI allows); otherwise prompt 'locked-off tripod shot'
ai_notes: Runway: write 'locked' or 'mounted on a tripod' rather than 'static shot', avoid 'following'/'revealing', and set movement to zero in settings where possible (Runway-CameraControl2026). Never use negative phrasing like 'no camera movement' (Runway-Gen4Guide).
common_mistakes: fully frozen 2D frame looks like a slideshow
AI video drifts anyway - generate 2-s tests
check: Does the action inside the frame carry the interest?

name: Breathing drift (micro-move)
definition: A slow, small, organic wander of the frame - the signature of a living operator, not a planned move.
how: Two sines at a 1.3 ratio (rig.js drift). Keep amplitude below the threshold where it reads as a move.
purpose: keep still frames alive in animation and stills-based clips
avoid_when: comic freeze-frames, graphic/flat design pieces where stillness is the style
rig_js: cam.drift(t0, t1, amp=4-8)  // needs t1-t0 >= 4 s
html_25d: add sin(t)*0.004 to cam.x and sin(1.3t)*0.0025 to cam.y
ai_video_prompt: Subtle handheld feel, almost still camera.
wan_prompt: almost still camera, very subtle natural camera sway
luma_key: handheld (too strong for this - prefer prompt)
ai_notes: AI models tend to exaggerate 'handheld' - prefer 'almost still' wording.
common_mistakes: amp so large it becomes a sway that competes with the action
check: Viewer should not consciously notice it.

name: Pan (left/right)
parallax: none (nodal pan) - near and far move together
definition: Camera swivels left or right from a fixed position. Pan = the camera as an eye turning (curriculum 05).
how: Real: fluid head, ideally nodal. Ease in/out. Avoid medium speeds that strobe at 24 fps (curriculum 05 §1.3).
purpose: follow a look or a moving subject, connect two things in one space, survey
use_when: a character looks off-screen and we turn to see
following a walker from a fixed point
avoid_when: you want the viewer to feel physically present (use truck/dolly - parallax)
rig_js: Build the scene with all layers at --d:1 (no parallax), s >= 960/(960-|Δpx|), then cam.move(t,dur,{px:+Δ},'power2.inOut'). With mixed --d it becomes a truck.
html_25d: Not a true 2.5D move (no parallax). Translate the whole image (CSS) or set FOCUS so depth offsets are ~0.
ai_video_prompt: The camera pans slowly from left to right across the shop, revealing the counter.
wan_prompt: slow pan right, camera turns from the window to the counter
kling_setting: Comfy/Kling doc: 'tilt' = rotation in the horizontal plane (-left/+right) - i.e. Kling 'tilt' is our pan. Verify with a 2-s test.
ai_notes: Veo lists 'Pan (left/right)'. Vendor axis names disagree (Comfy-KlingCameraNode).
speed_guide: slow: an object should take ≥ 5-7 s to cross the frame at 24 fps; otherwise go to a whip (CRAFT, curriculum 05)
common_mistakes: judder at medium speed
pan with no destination (ends on nothing)
check: Start frame and end frame are both composed.

name: Tilt (up/down)
definition: Camera pitches up or down from a fixed position.
how: Reveal height or connect top and bottom of a subject; ease both ends.
purpose: reveal height (a tall figure, a building), read a person head-to-toe, look up to sky
emotional_effect: tilt up: aspiration/awe; tilt down: deflation/grounding [CRAFT]
use_when: building or product vertical reveal (strong in 9:16)
avoid_when: when the viewer should feel the camera rise physically (pedestal)
rig_js: All layers --d:1, s >= 540/(540-|Δpy|), cam.move(t,dur,{py:+Δ},'sine.inOut')
html_25d: Translate the image vertically; not a parallax move.
ai_video_prompt: The camera tilts up slowly from her shoes to her face as she puts on sunglasses.
wan_prompt: slow tilt up from feet to face
kling_setting: Comfy/Kling doc: 'pan' = rotation in the vertical plane (-down/+up) - Kling 'pan' is our tilt. Test first.
speed_guide: 2-4 s for a body; slower for architecture
common_mistakes: tilting across nothing (empty wall)
check: Begins and ends on meaning.

name: Roll / Dutch move
definition: The frame rotates around the lens axis; a static roll = Dutch angle (angle.dutch).
how: Slow roll into a canted frame, or a fast roll for disorientation/transition.
purpose: world tips over - unease, intoxication, dream, transition
emotional_effect: instability; multi-axis rotation raises motion-sickness risk more than single-axis (KeshavarzRiecke2015) [EVIDENCE for sickness, not for emotion]
avoid_when: combined with handheld shake + forward motion on phone full screen (sickness risk)
rig_js: cam.move(t,dur,{rot:6, s: >= cos θ + 1.78·sin θ},'sine.inOut') - .cam rotates around 960,540; raise s so rotated edges stay covered (bg images have 12% slack only)
html_25d: CSS rotate on the canvas wrapper + scale up by the same coverage rule
ai_video_prompt: The camera slowly rolls clockwise until the corridor is tilted.
wan_prompt: camera slowly rolls clockwise, tilted horizon
speed_guide: slow roll 3-8° over 1.5-3 s; transition roll 90-180° in 6-10 F
common_mistakes: edges/black corners show
roll too subtle to read
check: No uncovered corners at max rotation.

name: Dolly in / push-in
parallax: yes - near things grow faster than far
definition: The camera physically moves toward the subject. Unlike a zoom, perspective and background relations change (Runway-CameraControl2026; Google-VeoPromptGuide).
how: Track/dolly/slider/gimbal. Speed = emotional weight: slow 3-5%/s scale for thought, 10-20%/s for realisation (curriculum 05, CRAFT).
purpose: 'this matters' - growing importance, entering a character's mind, focusing on a product
emotional_effect: a moving (Steadicam) approach produced stronger motor-cortex desynchronisation and was described as most like a person approaching than a zoom of the same room (Heimann2019) [EVIDENCE, low-medium]
use_when: a realisation, a decision, a line that lands
avoid_when: the move ends before anything happens
rig_js: cam.move(t, 2-4, {s: s0+0.1…0.4, px: subjectX, py: eyeY}, 'sine.inOut') with layers at --d .8 / 1 / 1.3 so it reads as a dolly
html_25d: clip-25d.html: zoom 1.08 → 1.22 with FOCUS at the subject's depth (subject stays, background slides) - template default
ai_video_prompt: Slow push-in on her face as she reads the letter.
wan_prompt: slow dolly in toward [subject], the camera moves closer, background parallax
kling_setting: zoom axis is focal length (optical) per Comfy doc - for a dolly prefer Master Shot 'move forward…' or prompt wording
ai_notes: Runway's model prompt: move + speed + subject + reason (Runway-CameraControl2026). Veo best-practice example: slow dolly in on the subject. Luma's learning hub conflates push-in with zoom - specify 'camera moves closer'.
speed_guide: slow 3-5 % scale/s; motivated 6-10 %/s; settle 6-12 F before a cut (GUIDE.md)
common_mistakes: linear (no ease) - looks mechanical
push on an empty moment
AI: push becomes a zoom with warping edges
check: Name the beat the push lands on; is the eye already where the push is going (Loschky2015)?

name: Dolly out / pull-out / pull-back reveal
definition: Camera moves away from the subject, widening the context.
how: Often starts close and ends wide, revealing new information (a crowd, the emptiness, the real situation).
purpose: reveal context, isolation, ending, irony (subject smaller than they think)
use_when: reveal the scale of a problem
subtext: she says 'I'm fine' while the camera leaves her small (curriculum 05)
avoid_when: opening a hook on a phone (the subject shrinks while attention is lowest)
rig_js: cam.move(t, 3-6, {s: lower}, 'sine.inOut')
html_25d: zoom 1.22 → 1.08 (reverse template)
ai_video_prompt: Slow pull-out from her face to reveal she is alone in an empty theatre.
wan_prompt: slow dolly out, camera moves backward revealing the room
kling_setting: Master Shot 'move down and zoom out' is the nearest preset
ai_notes: Describe what the end frame reveals (Runway-CameraControl2026: describe what each stage reveals).
common_mistakes: AI invents inconsistent new surroundings at the edges as it reveals
check: End frame composed and meaningful.

name: Truck / crab (lateral move)
definition: Camera moves sideways parallel to the subject.
how: Dolly track, slider, car, or walking gimbal. Put something in the foreground to sell it.
purpose: walk alongside a character, reveal from behind a pillar, show a row of products
avoid_when: Bordwell's 'slider' drift that promises a reveal and never delivers (Bordwell2023-CalmCamera)
rig_js: cam.move(t,dur,{px:+Δ},'power2.inOut') with s >= 960/(960-|Δ|) and layers --d .8/1/1.3
html_25d: clip-25d.html cam.x sweep (-0.06 → +0.06) with FOCUS at the far background (everything nearer slides)
ai_video_prompt: The camera trucks right along the display shelves, glasses sliding past in the foreground.
wan_prompt: camera moves sideways to the right, lateral tracking shot, parallax
speed_guide: match the walker's speed; product line-up ~1 item per 0.6-1 s
common_mistakes: no foreground - reads as a pan
rig.js: px move at s=1 does nothing (clamped)
check: Is there a reveal or a companion at the end?

name: Pedestal (up/down)
definition: Whole camera rises or lowers without tilting.
how: Studio pedestal, jib with level head, or gimbal. Often follows a character standing/sitting.
purpose: match a character's change of height; reveal over a counter/wall
emotional_effect: rising: lift, hope; lowering: settle, gravity [CRAFT]
use_when: customer stands up from the eye-test chair
rising over a foreground edge to reveal
avoid_when: a tilt would do (no parallax needed)
rig_js: cam.move(t,dur,{py:+Δ}) with s >= 540/(540-|Δ|) and parallax layers
html_25d: cam.y sweep with FOCUS at the background
ai_video_prompt: The camera rises straight up over the counter to reveal the optician working behind it.
wan_prompt: camera rises vertically, pedestal up, revealing
ai_notes: Veo lists 'Pedestal (up/down)'. Models often add a tilt.
common_mistakes: pedestal with tilt mixed unintentionally
check: Horizon stays level during the move.

name: Crane / jib / boom
axis: arc through space, usually y+z with tilt
definition: Camera on an arm sweeps up/down/over, usually combining pedestal, push and tilt.
how: Rise and tilt down to keep the subject; or descend from overview into the scene (Bound for Glory began a Steadicam shot from a crane that came down, per Wiki-Steadicam).
purpose: open or close a big scene, god's-eye perspective, rising hope / descending dread
use_when: show a character's place in the larger world

examples.note: Opening move: crane jibbed down, then Garrett Brown stepped off and walked the camera through the set with the Steadicam (per Wikipedia/Garrett Brown summaries)

rig_js: cam.move(t,dur,{py:-Δ, s: s0-0.2}) - py and s together (GUIDE.md); for a 'crane down into scene' reverse it
html_25d: zoom out + cam.y up together
ai_video_prompt: Start low behind the ledge on a lone figure, then crane up over the ridge to reveal the canyon below.
wan_prompt: crane shot rising up and over, revealing the town below
kling_setting: Master Shot 'move forward and zoom up' approximates
ai_notes: Runway's multi-stage example above is from Runway-CameraControl2026.
common_mistakes: crane for its own sake
check: Does the height change change the meaning?

name: Arc / orbit
parallax: strong, opposite directions in front of and behind the subject
definition: Camera travels on a curve around the subject while keeping it framed. Bordwell notes the arc/'roundy-round' (Kwapis' term) as a contemporary TV tic, e.g. E.R. to convey time slipping away (Bordwell2023-CalmCamera).
how: Arc track or gimbal walk; subject stays centred while background swings.
purpose: make the subject the centre of the world; romance, heroism, product 360

examples.note: Circling camera during surgery to convey time slipping away (Kwapis, reported by Bordwell)

rig_js: No true orbit in 2D. Fake: cam.move px +Δ while the fg layer (--d 1.3) and bg (--d .8) slide opposite ways relative to the subject + slight s change; or swap puppet views (front→3/4→side) on the move
html_25d: BEST tool for a small orbit: clip-25d.html cam.x sweep with FOCUS = subject depth -> subject stays put, background slides one way, foreground the other. Keep |cam| ≤ ~0.06-0.08 before edges tear (curriculum 10 §4.3: ≤ ~8%)
ai_video_prompt: The camera slowly orbits around the pair of glasses on a marble plinth, keeping them centred.
wan_prompt: camera orbits slowly around [subject], arc shot, subject stays centered
ai_notes: Veo lists 'Arc shot'. Orbit around eyewear is a high-risk morph shot (temples/lenses deform) - check every frame; prefer 2.5D or real photos from several angles (house rule: real glasses from several angles).
speed_guide: 10-30° per 3 s for drama; full 360 only for product
common_mistakes: AI product melts mid-orbit
arc on dialogue for no reason
check: Product shape identical at start, middle, end frames.

name: Tracking / follow (behind or beside)
definition: Camera moves with a moving subject, keeping distance. 'Follow' is a semantic primitive defined by the subject, which geometry-only trackers miss (Lin2025-CameraBench).
how: Gimbal/Steadicam/car; from behind (mystery, journey) or side (companionship).
purpose: journey, pursuit, immersion in a character's path
rig_js: Character walk(…) + cam.move with ease 'none' at the walk speed (curriculum 05: linear only for follows)
html_25d: not suitable (subject must move)
ai_video_prompt: Tracking shot following behind a girl as she runs through a market, camera at shoulder height, smooth gimbal.
wan_prompt: tracking shot following behind [subject], smooth
ai_notes: Veo 3.1 guide lists tracking shots among camera-movement terms (Google-VeoPromptGuide search summary). Avoid saying 'following' if you want a locked camera (Runway).
common_mistakes: subject drifts in frame because camera speed ≠ walk speed
check: Subject's frame position stable (or changes on purpose).

name: Leading track (camera backs away in front)
axis: translate backward with an approaching subject
definition: Camera moves backward ahead of a walking subject, face toward camera.
how: Gimbal/Steadicam operator walks backward; keep distance constant.
purpose: walk-and-talk, confident entrance, fashion walk
avoid_when: the destination is the point (use follow from behind)
rig_js: front-facing walk puppet + cam s held, py constant; or scale the character up slowly with the bg layer scrolling down
html_25d: not suitable
ai_video_prompt: A woman in sunglasses walks toward the camera down a sunny street; the camera tracks backward in front of her at the same speed.
wan_prompt: camera moves backward in front of the walking woman, she walks toward camera
ai_notes: Steadicam encouraged walk-and-talk staging (Kwapis via Bordwell2023-CalmCamera).
common_mistakes: AI makes the walker moonwalk / feet slide
check: Feet contact the ground without sliding.

name: Handheld
definition: Camera held by hand/shoulder; visible human instability.
how: Shoulder rig; in 2D drift amp 6-12 + small occasional shakes.
purpose: documentary truth, nerves, chaos, POV
emotional_effect: viewpoint jitter added to forward motion raised both vection and motion sickness in lab studies (KeshavarzRiecke2015) [EVIDENCE]
avoid_when: long full-screen phone sequences with forward motion + shake

examples.note: Bordwell cites its free camera with 'wobblecam' trembling and line-jumping

rig_js: cam.drift(t0,t1,8-12) + cam.shake(t,.2,3-5,12) at story beats
html_25d: add noise to cam.x/y (±0.003) - fake
ai_image_prompt: handheld camera, slight motion blur, candid
ai_video_prompt: Handheld documentary-style shot, slight natural shake, following the argument at close range.
wan_prompt: handheld camera, slight shake, documentary style
ai_notes: Veo: 'Handheld or shaky cam'. Runway: 'handheld, with slight unsteadiness' adds texture.
speed_guide: shake amp ≤ 1% of frame width for drama
common_mistakes: too much shake (unwatchable on phones)
uniform random shake with no rhythm of breathing/steps
check: Can you still read faces and text?

name: Steadicam / gimbal float
definition: Body-worn or motorised stabiliser: an operator walks anywhere but the image floats. Invented by Garrett Brown (patent filed 1974; first feature Bound for Glory; used in Rocky's steps run) (Wiki-Steadicam).
how: Plan a walking path; ease at starts/stops; keep horizon level.
purpose: long takes, following through spaces, ghost-like presence
emotional_effect: embodied presence: Steadicam clips evoked stronger motor-cortex desynchronisation than still or zoom and were described as most like a person approaching (Heimann2019) [EVIDENCE, low-medium]

examples.note: Steadicam used for the training runs incl. the museum steps (per Steadicam histories)
Apparent one-shot built from long takes; camera passed between rigs mid-shot; planned like a second script

rig_js: sequence of cam.move segments with 'sine.inOut' + light drift; no shake
html_25d: short push/orbit combos
ai_video_prompt: Smooth gimbal shot gliding through the shop door and past the shelves toward the counter.
wan_prompt: smooth gimbal shot moving forward through the doorway
speed_guide: walking pace ~1-1.4 m/s; ease in/out each segment
common_mistakes: gimbal too perfect - floaty 'video game' feel; add slight drift
check: Every segment has a destination frame.

name: Zoom (optical)
definition: Changing focal length from a fixed position; magnifies without perspective change (Google-VeoPromptGuide: 'the camera itself doesn't move'; Runway: 'without parallax').
how: Zoom lens; smooth servo. In 2D: scale without layer parallax.
purpose: observational/reportage feel, attention pointer, 70s/documentary style
emotional_effect: optical, detached 'looking closer' rather than 'stepping closer' [CRAFT]
zoom produced weaker motor-cortex response than a Steadicam approach (Heimann2019) [EVIDENCE, low-medium]
rig_js: Scene with all layers --d:1, then cam.move(t,dur,{s:+Δ}). With mixed --d layers it becomes a dolly.
html_25d: CSS scale on the flat image, or zoom uniform with FOCUS so depth offsets are 0
ai_video_prompt: A slow, dramatic zoom in on a mysterious, ancient compass lying on a dusty map.
wan_prompt: slow zoom in on [subject]
kling_setting: zoom (Comfy doc: negative narrows FOV = zoom in? verify sign with a test)
ai_notes: Veo example quoted verbatim in ai_video_prompt (Google-VeoPromptGuide).
common_mistakes: zoom used when a dolly is meant
2D 'zoom' on a low-res image - pixelation
check: Was 'no perspective change' the intent?

name: Snap / crash zoom
definition: A zoom in a few frames with a hard stop.
how: 4-8 F, power3.out / expo.out; often with a sound hit.
purpose: comedy beat, shock realisation, action punctuation
use_when: reaction gags, hook moments in short-form
rig_js: cam.move(t, 6*R.F, {s:+0.6…1.0, px, py}, 'power3.out') + sfx hit
html_25d: zoom jump over 4-8 frames
ai_video_prompt: Sudden crash zoom onto his shocked face.
wan_prompt: sudden fast zoom in on the face
ai_notes: Runway lists 'crash zoom'. AI often renders it as a slow zoom - do it in the edit instead (punch-in crop).
common_mistakes: no settle - the frame keeps drifting after the snap
check: Hard stop + hold ≥ 12 F.

name: Dolly zoom (vertigo / contra-zoom)
parallax: inverted - background stretches or compresses while subject size stays
definition: Dolly and zoom in opposite directions keep the subject's size while the background perspective changes; constant width W at distance d = W/(2·tan(FOV/2)) (Wiki-DollyZoom).
how: Real: track + zoom matched. 2D: background layer scales while camera pulls back on the subject.
purpose: realisation, dread, 'the floor drops', comic fake bravery
use_when: once per film, at the realisation beat
avoid_when: more than once per piece; on product shots (meaningless)

examples.note: Devised by second-unit cameraman Irmin Roberts for Hitchcock
Brody realises there is a shark on the beach
Comic use - bravery fails when the shotgun jams

rig_js: cam.vertigo(t, .8-1.5, '#bgLayer', .2-.4)
html_25d: approximate: grow zoom only for depth < FOCUS (background) while subject layer fixed - needs a separated subject cutout
ai_video_prompt: Dolly zoom on the man's face: he stays the same size while the corridor behind him stretches away.
wan_prompt: dolly zoom vertigo effect, background stretches while the face stays the same size
kling_setting: horizontal 0, zoom + forward master shot - unreliable
ai_notes: Veo: 'Vertigo effect (dolly zoom)' listed under lens terms; Luma key dolly_zoom. Untested here - do it in rig.js/2.5D where it is deterministic.
common_mistakes: subject size drifts (not matched)
overuse
check: Subject size constant within ~3%.

name: Whip pan
definition: A pan so fast the image smears into streaks; often used as a transition, cutting in the blur.
how: 6-8 F move, expo.inOut + directional blur; cut at the blurred middle to the next scene moving the same way.
purpose: energy, time/place jump, comedy
use_when: snapping attention to a new speaker
rig_js: cam.move(t, 7*R.F, {px:+600}, 'expo.inOut') + layer --blur 12px at the midpoint; R.cut at the blur peak; next scene starts with a matching whip-out
html_25d: CSS translate + blur; cut in the blur
ai_video_prompt: Whip pan to the right to the shop door.
wan_prompt: fast whip pan to the right, motion blur
kling_setting: tilt (Kling's yaw per Comfy doc) high value
ai_notes: Veo lists 'Whip pan'. Better done in the edit than generated.
common_mistakes: direction mismatch between whip-out and whip-in
check: Both halves move the same direction and speed.

name: Drone / aerial move
definition: Aerial camera flight: fly-over, rising reveal, top-down rise, orbit of a landmark.
how: Plan altitude, direction and the reveal; slow and steady reads 'cinematic'.
purpose: geography, scale, chapter openers
rig_js: painted wide plate + cam.move py/s; or 2.5D on an aerial still
html_25d: aerial still + zoom 1.08→1.18 + cam.y drift (forward flight feel)
ai_image_prompt: aerial drone photo of a coastal town at golden hour
ai_video_prompt: Sweeping aerial drone shot flying over a tropical island chain.
wan_prompt: aerial drone shot flying forward over [place], smooth
kling_setting: Master Shot 'move forward and zoom up'
ai_notes: Veo example quoted. Wide aerials hide AI artefacts; watch for fake signs/text.
common_mistakes: generic drone filler with no story purpose
check: What new information does the flight reveal?

name: FPV / bolt-cam fly-through
definition: First-person-view drone or high-speed rig (Luma key 'bolt_cam') flying fast and close through gaps, doors, between objects.
how: One continuous path through 3-5 'gates' (door, shelf gap, window); speed ramps.
purpose: energy, spatial tour in seconds, 'impossible' camera
emotional_effect: fast forward optic flow + rotation + jitter is the high-risk recipe for motion sickness (KeshavarzRiecke2015) [EVIDENCE]
use_when: shop tour in 5 s, event openers
rig_js: not practical in 2D; use AI video or real FPV
html_25d: no
ai_video_prompt: Fast FPV drone shot flying through the shop door, weaving between display shelves and stopping on the counter.
wan_prompt: fast FPV drone flying forward through the door between shelves
ai_notes: AI tends to morph geometry at FPV speed; plan cuts at 1.5-2 s.
speed_guide: ramp: fast through gaps, slow at the destination
common_mistakes: no destination; nausea
check: Ends on a held, readable frame.

name: Rack focus (focus pull as a move)
definition: Shift sharp focus from one plane to another within a shot; attention follows sharpness.
how: Pull focus over .6-1 s motivated by a look, sound or action.
purpose: redirect attention without cutting; reveal a second subject
html_25d: blur by |depth - focus| (depth map) and animate focus value
ai_image_prompt: shallow depth of field, foreground in focus, background soft
ai_video_prompt: A medium shot of a detective's hand in the foreground, holding a single, spent bullet casing; focus shifts to the man behind.
wan_prompt: rack focus from the glasses in the foreground to the woman's face behind
ai_notes: Veo lists 'Rack focus' (example quoted, extended with the focus shift). AI rack focus is unreliable - do it in rig.js/2.5D.
common_mistakes: rack without motivation
both planes equally bright - no target
check: Is there a reason to look at the new plane at that moment?

name: Impact shake
definition: A brief, decaying camera shake for impacts, explosions, slams.
how: 0.3-0.6 s, amplitude decays to zero, synced to a sound hit.
purpose: physical impact, scare punctuation
html_25d: random cam offsets decaying
ai_video_prompt: The camera shakes briefly as the door slams.
wan_prompt: brief camera shake on impact
common_mistakes: shake without sound
check: Synced to an audio transient (FX.md).

name: Reveal past foreground (wipe-by)
definition: Camera moves so a foreground object uncovers the subject (or covers it - Bordwell's 'peekaboo' when it hides the subject).
how: Start occluded, truck/pedestal until clear; or use the occluder as a natural cut point (wipe transition).
purpose: surprise, discovery, seamless transitions
use_when: product reveal from behind a shelf
hiding a cut between two AI clips
avoid_when: the reveal is nothing (Bordwell's slider complaint)

examples.note: Bordwell cites it as an early example of the 'peekaboo' reframing tic (subject hidden by drift)

rig_js: fg occluder layer --d 1.4; cam.move px across; or R.cut when the occluder fills the frame
html_25d: cam.x sweep with a near-depth occluder in the image
ai_video_prompt: The camera slides out from behind a dark shelf to reveal the new collection lit on the table.
wan_prompt: camera slides sideways from behind a shelf revealing [subject]
common_mistakes: reveal without payoff
check: Is the payoff worth the wait?
